DGO Digital Operations

Flow Studio Handbook

Build a set of Power Automate actions, copy them, and paste them straight into the modern designer. No import, no retyping.

Three ways to run it

Same tool, same generator, three deliveries. Pick whichever is nearest to hand.

Download

The single file

Save dist/flow-studio.html anywhere and open it. No server, no install, no network — it works offline and on a machine that has never seen the repository.

This is the one to hand to someone who just needs to build a flow.

Repo

Served from source

From the repository root:

npx http-server . -p 8080

Then open /tools/flow-studio.html. Use this when you are editing the generator, since it picks up changes on reload.

Platform

Inside DGO

Sidebar → SYSTEM → Flow Studio, or go straight to #/flow-studio.

Administration-tier route: available to systemAdmin, userAdmin and the admin persona. Operators, directors and viewers do not see it.

The short path

From a cold start to actions sitting in your flow. This is a real sequence — the steps only work in this order.

  1. 1 Load a blueprint

    Top of the plan column: pick DGO endpoint request handler from Start from a blueprint… and choose your endpoint below it. You get a timestamp, a typed request, a switch over every action that endpoint declares, and an enveloped response per branch.

  2. 2 Check the findings

    The paste bar is pinned along the bottom. It lists anything blocking in red, anything worth checking in amber, and notes in blue. Nothing generates while a blocking issue stands.

  3. 3 Copy for the designer

    Press Copy for the designer. Use Show JSON first if you want to read what you are about to paste.

  4. 4 Paste into the flow

    In the Power Automate designer, click the + where the actions belong and choose Paste an action. The whole set arrives at once.

The screen

One screen, two columns. Nothing is hidden behind a tab.

The plan column left, always visible

Everything the flow contains, in order, with the trigger as its first row. Drag a row to reorder it — including into and out of a branch. Containers such as Condition and Switch collapse with the twisty. Each row carries move, duplicate and remove, and shows the name the action will actually paste as when de-duplication has changed it.

The + between rows how you add anything

Hover between two rows, or inside an empty branch, and press the +. A palette opens with search already focused: type, use ↑ ↓, press Enter. The action lands exactly where you pressed — there is no separate destination to set.

The working column right

Whatever is selected: an action's fields, the trigger, the importer, or the payload check. Expression chips appear under whichever field you are typing in. Schema fields carry an Infer from a sample payload box.

The paste bar pinned to the bottom

Copy for the designer is always reachable and confirms on the button itself. Findings sit beside it. JSON shows exactly what will go on the clipboard.

What will trip you up

Six things that are not obvious and cost real time when you meet them for the first time.

Firefox cannot receive the paste

Firefox does not expose navigator.clipboard.readText() to web pages, so the designer falls back to reading its own origin's storage — which nothing outside make.powerautomate.com can write. Use Chrome or Edge. The page says so when opened in Firefox.

Several actions arrive wrapped in a Scope

A single paste carries exactly one root action, so more than one gets wrapped. Delete the Scope afterwards if you do not want the grouping — the designer keeps its contents.

Initialize variable forces several pastes

The workflow service rejects an InitializeVariable anywhere but the top level, so it cannot go inside the Scope wrapper. Mix one into a plan and the output splits into numbered parts — paste them in the order shown.

Connector actions land unbound

The generator has no access to your tenant's connection ids, so SharePoint, Outlook, Approvals and Teams actions paste without a connection. Pick it on each one after pasting. This is expected, not a fault.

Triggers cannot be pasted at all

The designer's paste path creates actions only — a trigger is not in that graph. Add it in the designer yourself. Copy workflow definition is not a way round this: Power Automate's code view is read-only, so that export is for Logic Apps or for a flow inside a solution package, not for pasting back into a cloud flow.

Braces around an array break it

@{body('Get_items')} interpolates, and interpolation turns the value into text. Fields that consume an array or object need the value itself: @body('Get_items'). The studio flags this, because at run time it fails as a type error naming neither the field nor the missing braces.

Building one from scratch

When no blueprint fits, work in this order — it keeps the reference errors down.

  1. 1 Add the actions

    Press the + where the action belongs and pick it from the palette. Container actions — Condition, Switch, Apply to each, Scope — grow their own branches, each with its own + inside.

  2. 2 Name them before you reference them

    Each row shows the name the action will actually carry, in monospace. Two actions named Compose become Compose and Compose_2, and the second is highlighted so you can see it was renamed. Reference that name, not what you typed.

  3. 3 Fill the fields

    The expression chips under the field you are in insert at the caret. On Parse JSON, open Infer from a sample payload, paste a real payload and press Infer schema rather than writing one by hand.

  4. 4 Set the ordering where it matters

    Actions chain by default. For a failure branch, pick an earlier action under Run after and tick Failed and TimedOut — two actions after the same one, on opposite statuses. Chaining a failure response to a success response never fires: a failed step leaves the success step Skipped, and Skipped is not Failed.

When something goes wrong

What you seeWhat it means
Paste an action is greyed out The clipboard does not hold a payload the designer recognises. Press Copy for the designer again, in the same browser, and do not copy anything else in between.
Nothing renders at all You opened tools/flow-studio.html from file://. That version needs a server. Use dist/flow-studio.html instead.
Not generating yet A blocking issue stands. The red panel names the action and the field.
The flow saves, then fails at run time Usually an unbound connector connection, or an expression referencing an action name that does not exist in the target flow. The amber findings list both before you paste.
A connector action is rejected on save The operation or a parameter name has changed in your tenant. Open the real action's code view and bring it in through Import from designer.
You suspect the payload format itself Press Check payload. Put an action in a Scope in your own designer, copy the Scope, paste it in, and the tool names every difference between what your designer produced and what it generates — or confirms they match, which points the search at the action definitions instead.
Your plan disappeared Plans live in that browser's local storage, per surface. Use Save plan for anything you want to keep or hand to someone else.

Nothing in Flow Studio talks to a network. Plans stay in your browser and go nowhere else.
